post.caption: Brooch comes from a word for skewer. It comes from French broche, a pointed tool like an awl. Behind that is Latin broccus, meaning pointed or projecting. Modern French broche still means both a brooch and a roasting spit. Brooch and broach began as one word, with two spellings later. To broach a subject began as tapping a cask. Brochure meant a stitched work when it arrived in English in 1748. Broccoli is a cousin, from Italian for a shoot or small nail. The Hunterston Brooch was made around the year 700. Two centuries later someone scratched the owner's name on its back.
